mapping.title: Studio is an app-wide viewport switched by its icon, other modules keep running
mapping.note: Reinforces R-7: module switching must be a viewport swap over live state, so Studio's document set and dock layout must survive a switch to another module and back. The PaneType::StudioViewport recommendation is what makes that survivable.

mapping.title: Arbitrary editor windows inside the main window, each with tabs
mapping.note: This requirement CHANGED the centre region of this proposal. The centre is not 'one or more viewers'; it is an unbounded egui_tiles tree of editor GROUPS, each group a tab stack, VS Code style. See regions[centre].editor_group_model.

mapping.title: Tabs inside Studio for different files and projects
Panels dock to any of four edges, tabbed, reorganisable, with a deliberated default
Everything reachable from the top menu bar
mapping.note: Every panel action, every dock gesture and every panel-open must be a command in the existing command_registry.rs, which already backs top_menu_bar.rs and command_palette.rs. No Studio surface may own an action that has no command. Stated as a hard constraint in dock_model.constraints.

mapping.title: Tooltips everywhere, generated from captures
mapping.note: Density interacts with tooltips: at the field densities proposed here, the label is often abbreviated, so the tooltip carries the full vendor-written parameter description plus its real range and unit. That makes tooltips load-bearing rather than decorative in dense panels.

mapping.title: Every numeric field is a scrubbable value control
mapping.note: Two consequences for docking, both addressed explicitly rather than left to implementation: gesture ownership, and panel density as a sizing constraint.

mapping.title: Notes embeds Studio documents
mapping.note: Out of scope for the dock architecture beyond this: an embedded Studio view inside Notes gets NO edge docks, only the centre viewport plus the context bar. The dock model must therefore be able to render with all four edges absent.

mapping.title: Scope boundary by document type
mapping.note: This proposal's seven document types are exactly OUI-010's list. If OUI-010 is not confirmed, the seven default layouts are the artefact that changes.

deduplication_method.principle: Applied the same rule the capability registry applies to capabilities: a Studio panel is one entity if the vendor surfaces it merges answer the same operator question about the same object at the same moment. Vendor surfaces that differ only by (a) document type, (b) orientation, (c) preset kind, (d) which of several near-identical effect kinds is being edited, or (e) which vendor shipped it, are ONE Studio panel with a parameter, not several panels.
collapse_ratios: InDesign ships 34 resource variants of ONE Control Panel and 9 XP*PanelViews for the nine transparency effect kinds. 43 captured surfaces collapse into 2 Studio panels (context-bar, effect-controls).

Photoshop ships textcharacter, textparagraph, textcharstyle, textparastyle, textglyphspanel as 5 panels; Illustrator ships Character, Paragraph, AdobeCharStyles, AdobeParaStyles, AdobeOpenTypeFont, AdobeAltGlyphsPanel, AdobeHorizontalTabPanel, AdobeVerticalTabPanel as 8. 13 captured surfaces collapse into 5 Studio panels (character, paragraph, text-styles, opentype, glyphs) plus tabs-indents.

Photoshop's swatches / gradients / patterns / customshapes / styles / toolpresets / brushpresets sit adjacent inside one tab group in every shipped workspace. 7 captured surfaces collapse into swatches + preset-library + brushes = 3.
Premiere ships TitlerProperties, TitlerStyles, TitlerTools, TitlerActions, TitlerEditor and Graphics as 6 surfaces for one job. They collapse into graphics-templates = 1.
Illustrator AdobeSeparationPreview + AdobeFlatteningPreview, InDesign InkMgrPanel + ColorPanel(PrintUI), plus Affinity's soft-proof and 32-bit preview entries collapse into print-preview = 1.
Dreamweaver's 60 property inspectors are NOT 60 panels. They are 60 BINDINGS into one slot. They collapse into properties = 1 plus 60 binding declarations.
deduplication_method.honest_caveat: 75 is the count of panel IDENTITIES. It is not a count of screens: preset-library, effect-controls, source-viewer, scopes and long-document each carry an internal mode/kind selector that in the vendor products was a separate panel. If the operator later rejects any of those five merges, the count rises by at most 17.

distinct_panels.name: Layers
distinct_panels.dedup_note: Dreamweaver's DOM tree is the same object: the document's node hierarchy. Bound as the web-document rendering of layers rather than a separate panel.

distinct_panels.name: Pages & Artboards

affinity: left-shelf Layout book member; artb workspace flag

distinct_panels.dedup_note: Pages (sequential, spread-aware) and Artboards (free-positioned) are one structure with a layout mode flag. InDesign's 6 Pages Panel variants are spread/master/alternate-layout modes of the same panel.

distinct_panels.name: Paths
distinct_panels.dedup_note: Kept separate from layers because in a raster document paths are a parallel, non-layer store. In a vector document paths ARE layers, so this panel is not offered there.

distinct_panels.name: States & Comps
distinct_panels.dedup_note: Layer Comps, Layer States and Snapshots are the same primitive: a named recall point over document state.

affinity: left-shelf Layout book member; Toc/Book strings

distinct_panels.name: Project Bin
distinct_panels.dedup_note: The set of things this document/project is made of. Premiere's Sequence Index folds in as a bin filter.

distinct_panels.name: Media Browser
distinct_panels.dedup_note: Distinct from project-bin: browses the FILESYSTEM, not the project. Premiere co-tabs them on the left in 10 of 13 workspaces where both appear, which is why they are adjacent by default but not merged.

distinct_panels.name: Library
distinct_panels.dedup_note: Libraries, Assets, Snippets and Stock are all 'reusable content from outside this document'. One panel, one source selector. 8 captured surfaces to 1.

distinct_panels.name: Preset Library
distinct_panels.dedup_note: Largest single merge: 12 captured surfaces to 1 kind-filtered browser. Justified by Photoshop's own workspace files, which place swatches/gradients/patterns adjacent inside one tab group in all 8 shipped workspaces. MUST support multiple simultaneous instances with different kind filters or this merge is a usability regression (see risks).

distinct_panels.name: Filter & Sort
distinct_panels.dedup_note: Premiere's Search panel is RIGHT in 7 of the 9 workspaces containing it; for a photo catalog the equivalent filter belongs on the top bar above the grid because it filters the viewport, not the selection.

distinct_panels.name: Properties
distinct_panels.dedup_note: THE contextual slot. Not a panel with fixed content: a host whose content is resolved by contextual_binding_rule. Premiere places Properties2 on the RIGHT in 15 of the 17 workspaces containing it - the single strongest placement fact in the whole corpus.

distinct_panels.name: Appearance
distinct_panels.dedup_note: Illustrator's Transparency panel (blend mode, opacity, knockout, opacity mask) merged in: it is the opacity section of the same fill/stroke/effect stack, and Illustrator's own Painting workspace orders Appearance, NamedStyle, Gradient, Transparency consecutively.

distinct_panels.name: Effect Controls

aftereffects: effect parameter UI implied by aftereffects_effects_catalogue.json

distinct_panels.dedup_note: The parameter editor for whatever effect stack the selection carries. InDesign's nine XP*PanelViews are nine sections of this one panel. Premiere's Essential Sound folds in because it is literally a selection-driven role editor for the selected audio clip.

distinct_panels.name: Adjustments
distinct_panels.dedup_note: The ordered non-destructive adjustment stack. For a photo document this IS the Develop column; for raster it is the adjustment-layer creator.

distinct_panels.name: Effects Browser
distinct_panels.dedup_note: Premiere docks the Effects browser LEFT in 8 of the 11 workspaces containing it, and Effect Controls elsewhere. Browse-left / inspect-right is a vendor-enforced split, not an invention.

distinct_panels.name: Text Styles
distinct_panels.dedup_note: 4 to 7 captured surfaces to 1. Affinity already ships character and paragraph styles as one Text Styles panel, which is the proof this merge is field-tested and not theoretical.

distinct_panels.name: Paragraph
distinct_panels.dedup_note: InDesign's Keeps, Justification and Paragraph Rules panels merged in as sections; they edit paragraph attributes and nothing else.

distinct_panels.name: Tabs & Indents
distinct_panels.dedup_note: Illustrator ships two panels that differ only by writing direction. One panel with an orientation control.

distinct_panels.name: Long Document
distinct_panels.dedup_note: 4 to 8 captured surfaces to 1 sectioned panel. Justified by Affinity's Layout workspace, which already places TOC and Index adjacent inside the same left-shelf book.

distinct_panels.name: Colour
distinct_panels.dedup_note: Illustrator's Colour Guide (harmony suggestions) merged in as a mode of the colour picker.

distinct_panels.name: Swatches
distinct_panels.dedup_note: Deliberately NOT merged into preset-library. Colour is selected far more often than any other preset kind and vendors give it its own always-open panel in 8/8 Photoshop and 12/12 Illustrator workspaces.

distinct_panels.name: Scopes
distinct_panels.dedup_note: Histogram, waveform, vectorscope and parade are display modes of one measurement surface.

distinct_panels.name: Info
distinct_panels.dedup_note: Photoshop's Measurement Log merged in: it is the persistent record of the same readout.

distinct_panels.name: Align & Distribute
distinct_panels.dedup_note: InDesign ships 14 numbered Alignment Panel resources for what is one panel whose control set varies with what is selected. That is the same one-slot-many-bindings pattern as the Control panel.

distinct_panels.name: Timeline
distinct_panels.dedup_note: NAME COLLISION with the existing shell PaneType::Timeline (an activity timeline). Studio's id must be studio.panel.timeline; the shell pane keeps its own id. Premiere places Timeline in the lower centre band in 16 of the 18 workspaces containing it, and Photoshop declares a bottom palette dock in 7 of 8 shipped workspaces, the animation palette being its occupant.

distinct_panels.name: Source Viewer
distinct_panels.dedup_note: 4 Premiere surfaces to 1 viewer with modes (source, reference, trim, multicam). Lives in the centre tile tree beside the program viewport, matching Premiere's centre-top placement in 8 of the workspaces containing it.

distinct_panels.name: Audio Mixer
distinct_panels.dedup_note: Clip mixer and track mixer are scope modes of one mixer.

distinct_panels.name: Audio Meters
distinct_panels.dedup_note: Premiere places MiniAudioMixer in a narrow far-right rail in 16 of 16 workspaces containing it - 100 percent. It is a rail occupant, not a dock tab.

distinct_panels.name: Graphics
distinct_panels.dedup_note: 6 captured surfaces to 1. Premiere's own newer Graphics panel already absorbed the five legacy Titler surfaces; the capture still ships both generations.

distinct_panels.name: Export

affinity: export options, export layers, export items, quick export (structural book members)

distinct_panels.dedup_note: 9 or more captured surfaces to 1. Affinity's whole Slice workspace is nothing but this panel, which is why the operator's rejection of persona switching matters: an entire persona existed to show one panel.

distinct_panels.name: Print Preview
distinct_panels.dedup_note: Separation preview, flattener preview, ink manager, soft proof and 32-bit preview are five views of one question: what will actually come out.

distinct_panels.name: Preflight
distinct_panels.dedup_note: Bottom dock, not right: it reports on the whole document, not on the selection. Dreamweaver docks its equivalents (nodeOutput, search) to a bottom panelframe in both shipped workspaces.

distinct_panels.name: Find & Replace
distinct_panels.dedup_note: Document-scoped find and replace over text AND object attributes. Distinct from the existing shell FindInFiles pane, which searches the repository filesystem.

distinct_panels.name: Generate
distinct_panels.policy_flag: Dreamweaver and Premiere captures carry an explicit excluded_ai policy; Illustrator and Photoshop captures do not. Whether Studio ships a Generate panel at all, and whether it routes to Handshake's own ModelRuntime rather than a vendor service, is an operator decision - see open_questions.

distinct_panels.name: Tools

affinity: tpnl tool panel with 143 tool ids in named groups

distinct_panels.dedup_note: Left rail occupant in 18 of 19 Premiere workspaces and in 8 of 8 Photoshop workspaces (dock anchor left, content 'palette toolbar'). Affinity's tpnl serialises tools as ordered named GROUPS, which is the flyout model.

distinct_panels.name: Context Bar

affinity: tbar context toolbar with named item groups

distinct_panels.dedup_note: Unanimous across every vendor with a workspace capture: exactly one top strip, single-occupant, resolved from the active tool and the current selection. It is a slot, not a tab stack.

distinct_panels.name: Brushes
distinct_panels.dedup_note: Photoshop's Brushes (presets) and Brush Settings (engine) are adjacent in all 8 shipped workspaces. One panel, presets list plus a settings section.

distinct_panels.name: Vectorise
distinct_panels.dedup_note: Illustrator dedicates an entire shipped workspace (Tracing) to this one panel plus its supporting set. Under this architecture it is a task-episodic panel that opens on the command and returns to the icon rail after, with no whole-UI switch.

distinct_panels.name: Mockup
distinct_panels.dedup_note: Kept as its own panel rather than folded into effect-controls because it is present in 11 of the 12 Illustrator workspaces, i.e. the vendor treats it as first-class, not as an effect parameter.

hard_facts: 8 of 8 workspaces declare a dock with anchor=top and content=control-bar; its occupant is panelid.static.options in every one.
8 of 8 declare anchor=left with content='palette toolbar'; panelid.static.toolbar is placed there.
8 of 8 declare anchor=right with content='palette toolbar'; this is where the palettes live.
7 of 8 declare anchor=bottom with content='palette' (Assisted is the exception, having only 3 docks total).

Workspaces additionally declare anchor=none docks marked is_closed=true - between 0 and 8 of them - which are the closed floating groups. This is the vendor's own evidence for a hidden-but-registered panel state distinct from 'not installed'.
The 37 native panel ids are stable: 24 of them appear in 7 or 8 of the 8 workspaces. Only assisted.toolbar (1), patchmatch (2), smartbrush (2) and learn (4) are workspace-specific.

The trailing group of the right dock is identically ordered in Graphic and Web, Painting and Photography: ... layers, channels, paths. This is the vendor's own default tab order for the structure group.
adjacency_pairs_observed: textcharacter + textparagraph + textparastyle + textcharstyle + textglyphspanel (all workspaces)
layers + channels + paths (Graphic and Web, Painting, Photography, Motion)

hard_facts: 41 surfaces appear in all 12 workspaces. ControlBar 12/12 and ToolBar 12/12: the top control bar and the left tool bar are structural, not optional.
Illustrator does not vary WHICH panels exist per workspace; it varies their ORDER and is_closed flag. 45 to 46 of the 52 surfaces are open in every non-Start workspace.
The leading entries of each workspace's surface list are the docked-visible group, and they differ per workspace in exactly the way a task expects:
Typography leads Character, Paragraph, AdobeOpenTypeFont, AdobeCharStyles, AdobeParaStyles.
Layout leads Character, Paragraph, AdobeOpenTypeFont, AdobeCharStyles, AdobeParaStyles, Export, Links.
Painting leads ControlBar, Basic, Navigator, Info, Appearance, NamedStyle, AdobeGradientEditor, Transparency, Transform, Align, Pathfinder.
Tracing leads ControlBar, Basic, Actions, Links, AdobeBrush, AdobeGradientEditor, Stroke, Appearance, Info, AdobeObjectAttributes, AdobeLayerPalette, NamedStyle, then Vectorize.
Printing and Proofing leads Transform, Align, Pathfinder, Artboards, AdobeLayerPalette, Links.
Web leads AdobeVariablesPanel, Actions, Info, Character, Paragraph, AdobeOpenTypeFont, Links.
Appearance, NamedStyle (Graphic Styles), Gradient and Transparency are consecutive in Painting - the evidence used to merge Transparency into Appearance.
Transform + Align + Pathfinder are consecutive in 5 of the 12 workspaces. They are the geometry triple.

vendor_workspace_evidence.source: installed_exports/indesign/offline/indesign_dialogs.json (390 dialogs and panels, 144192 nodes, 1778 view resource files)
hard_facts: No workspace layout file was captured for InDesign, so InDesign contributes BINDING evidence rather than PLACEMENT evidence.

34 distinct Control Panel resource variants ship (Control Panel#6101, #6201, #7401, #7501, #8201, #8203, #8205, #8301, #9001, #9105, #9205, #9305, #9405, #51201, #51701, #51805, #53401, #53705, #53805, #54901 and 14 more). One slot, 34 bound layouts, chosen by what is selected. This is the single largest piece of evidence that the contextual-slot model is what the field actually ships.

Numbered variant families beyond Control Panel: Alignment Panel 14, Paragraph Panel 13, Style Panel 10, Character Panel 9, Transform Panel 6, Text Wrap Panel 6, Pages Panel 6, Color Picker Panel 3, Find Change Format Panel 3, Hyperlinks Panel 2.

9 XP*PanelViews (BevelEmboss 1125 nodes, DropShadow 1005, DirectionalFeather 950, InnerShadow 940, Satin 610, InnerGlow 600, OuterGlow 550, GradientFeather 550, Feather 365) are nine effect-kind layouts for one Effects dialog surface.
31 distinct panel-owning plugins, which is the closest InDesign gets to a panel inventory.

vendor_workspace_evidence.derivation_note: Zone labels computed by walking each pane_path's Splitter(orient,place)/SubN chain to a normalised rect, renormalising to the workspace's own occupied extent, then bucketing: width<=0.12 is a rail; centroid x<0.25 LEFT, x>0.75 RIGHT; otherwise CENTRE-TOP or CENTRE-BOTTOM by centroid y. This is the richest placement evidence in the corpus because Premiere serialises the actual splitter tree.
hard_facts: Tools: LEFT-RAIL in 18 of 19 placements. A narrow rail, never a tab.
MiniAudioMixer: RIGHT-RAIL in 16 of 16 placements. 100 percent. A second narrow rail on the far right.
Properties2: RIGHT in 15 of 17 placements. Present in 17 of 19 workspaces.
Project: LEFT in 15 of 17 placements. Media Browser: LEFT in 11 of 13.
Effects (the browser): LEFT in 8 of 11 placements.
Search: RIGHT in 7 of 9 placements.
Color (Lumetri): RIGHT in 5 of 6. Essential Sound: RIGHT in 3 of 4.
Timeline: CENTRE-BOTTOM in 16 of 18 placements.
Program Monitor: CENTRE-TOP in 16 of 19. Source Monitor: CENTRE-TOP in 8, LEFT in 5.

Effect Controls: co-tabbed with Source Monitor rather than docked right - LEFT 5, CENTRE-TOP 4, RIGHT 1. The vendor disagrees with itself here: the legacy placement rides the source-viewer stack, the modern Properties2 placement is right. Studio follows the modern one.

The largest single tab stack in the corpus is ALLPANELS' right dock: Properties2, Effects, Info, Graphics, Essential Sound, Color, Search, MetadataEditor, UXP, MarkerList, History, Events, Timecode - 13 tabs in one group. Vendors do stack this deep.
vendor_workspace_evidence.conclusion: Browse-left, inspect-right, time-bottom, viewers-centre, tools and meters in narrow rails. This is Premiere's own layout law across 19 shipped workspaces, and it is the empirical basis for the Studio edge semantics.

hard_facts: The workspace file is literally a dock model: panelset > panelframe(dock=left|right|bottom, width=N) > panelcontainer(expanded, visible) > panel(id, showLabel, width, height). Handshake's dock model can be a near-direct port of this shape.
Developer docks: left width=245 holding site + snippets; left width=35 holding DW_CodeView_Toolbar (an icon rail, 32px panel inside a 35px frame); bottom holding search, nodeOutput, DWGit.
Standard docks: left width=35 icon rail; right holding site, CC Libraries, objects (Insert), assets, snippets, CSS Designer, DOM; bottom holding output and search.

31 registered panels, of which only 6 (Developer) and 12 (Standard) are docked in a shipped workspace. 19 to 25 registered panels are reachable but not docked by default - the vendor's own evidence that most panels are episodic.
The 'properties' panel is registered but docked in NEITHER shipped workspace, because it is the Property Inspector host bar, not a dock tab.
60 property inspectors, 60 of 60 carrying a binding declaration, 487 controls total.

tag_values_observed: concrete tags: audio, video, canvas, source, BASE, LINK, META, TITLE, button, input, div, span, UL, cfform, cfinput, cfselect, cftextarea, xsl:comment, XSL:IF, XSL:WHEN, XSL:FOR-EACH, MMTemplate:If, MM_REPEATEDREGION
binding_declaration_shape.priority_semantics_inferred: Higher wins. Proof inside the capture: spry_widget.htm binds tag=div at priority 1 (the catch-all for any Spry div) while spry_accordion.htm, spry_collapsiblepanel.htm, spry_tabbedpanels.htm, jQuery_accordion.htm, jQuery_slider.htm and jQuery_tabs.htm all bind tag=div at priority 50. The generic fallback is the low number; the specific widget is the high number. META is bound at 5 by meta.htm and at 6 by description.htm, keywords.htm, refresh.htm and viewport.htm, which are the refined variants - again higher-is-more-specific.

vendor_workspace_evidence.source: installed_exports/affinity/offline/affinity_tool_panel_registry.json workspaces[].workspace lshl / rshl / floa / tpnl / tbar
vendor_workspace_evidence.name_binding_caveat: The capture states that the 4CC panel ids are not bound to names in any shipped resource and refuses to guess. Everything below is STRUCTURAL and is quoted without asserting which panel a 4CC is.
hard_facts: The serialised model is: tbar (context toolbar with ordered item groups), tpnl (tool panel with ordered named groups), lshl (left shelf), rshl (right shelf), floa (floating books). A shelf contains 'book' entries; a book is a tab stack with itms plus a parallel hidd visibility array and a _sel active-tab marker.

Right shelf book counts: Vector 3, Pixel 3, Layout 3, Slice 2, Canva AI 3, Retouching 2, Colour Grading 2, Typography 3, Compositing 3. THREE stacked tab groups on the right is the modal answer - 6 of 9 workspaces.

Left shelf is EMPTY in Vector, Slice and Typography; present in Pixel, Layout, Canva AI, Retouching, Colour Grading, Compositing. A left browse dock is optional and document-type dependent, which is exactly how Studio treats it.
Retouching is the only workspace with a large floating set - 5 separate floating books plus help. Floating is a real, shipped state, not an edge case.

Slice is the extreme case: two right books containing 3 entries total and nothing else. An entire persona-adjacent workspace exists to show what is effectively one panel. This is the concrete cost of the persona model the operator rejected.
Typography workspace: 2 left books of 1 entry each and 3 right books of 1-2 entries each, all with hidd=1 (hidden). The workspace is almost entirely a set of hidden registrations.
The tool panel (tpnl) serialises tools as ordered GROUPS with optional names - e.g. one group of 24 shape tool ids, one group of 3 brush-family ids. That is the flyout structure, captured.

40798 capabilities across 9 apps. Domain vocabulary used verbatim by this proposal: cross_cutting 8357, color 7009, effects 4420, layout 4204, vector 3240, interop 2656, typography 2522, raster 2479, design_system 1511, automation 1261, web 1158, video 693, raw 398, prototype 365, motion 310, document_model 183, whiteboard 32.

kind=panel yields 814 rows, but inspection shows those rows are string-derived and include non-panels such as 'Top', 'Underline', 'Visible'. The registry's panel kind is NOT a usable panel inventory and was deliberately not used as the dedup input; the per-app panel captures were.

39144 of 40798 capabilities are single-app. Only 29 are shared by 6 apps and 6 by 7. The apps overlap far less at capability level than at panel level - which is why panel dedup (595 to 75, an 8:1 collapse) is far more aggressive than capability dedup.

document_primitives supplies the node-type vocabulary the contextual binding rule matches against: Document, TextNode, VectorNode, FrameNode, ComponentNode, InstanceNode, ComponentSetNode, SlotNode, SlideNode, TextPathNode, BooleanOperationNode, RectangleNode, EllipseNode, PolygonNode, StarNode, LineNode, HighlightNode, StampNode, WashiTapeNode, TransformGroupNode, SVG11 and more.

panel_classification.definition: Answers a question the operator has at essentially every moment in every document type. Docked and visible by default; never auto-hidden.
panel_classification.test_applied: Present and open in 7 or more of 8 Photoshop workspaces, or 11 or more of 12 Illustrator workspaces, or 15 or more of 19 Premiere workspaces, or present in a majority of Affinity shelves.

panel_classification.definition: Always relevant, but only inside certain document types. Present in the default layout for those types and absent - not merely collapsed - for the others.
panel_classification.test_applied: Vendor ships it only in the applications that own that document type, or the panel edits a primitive that does not exist in other types.

panel_classification.definition: Relevance is determined by what is currently selected, not by document type or by the operator. Resolved by contextual_binding_rule into a slot; appears and disappears with the selection.
panel_classification.test_applied: The vendor either ships multiple bound variants of it (InDesign numbered families, Dreamweaver inspectors) or its content is empty with no selection.
panel_classification.note: properties appears in both always_relevant and selection_contextual: the SLOT is always present, its OCCUPANT is contextual. That dual nature is the whole point of the design.

panel_classification.definition: Opened deliberately for a job, used, then closed. Lives in the icon rail by default and returns there when the job ends. This class is the direct replacement for Affinity's persona toggle: instead of switching the whole UI to expose one panel, the panel comes to the operator and then leaves.
panel_classification.test_applied: Registered by the vendor but not docked in the shipped default workspace (Dreamweaver: 19 to 25 of 31 panels), or the vendor dedicated an entire workspace or persona to it (Illustrator Tracing, Affinity Slice).

panel_classification.note: Each of the 75 distinct_panels entries carries exactly one classification field: always_relevant 16, document_type_specific 22, selection_contextual 18, task_episodic 19 = 75. The member lists above sum to 76 because 'properties' is deliberately listed in BOTH always_relevant and selection_contextual - its SLOT is always present, its OCCUPANT is contextual. Its entry-level classification is selection_contextual.

dock_model.summary: Five regions: four edge docks plus the centre. Each edge is a stack of GROUPS; each group is a TAB STACK; each tab is one panel instance. Two edges additionally carry a narrow outer RAIL that is a single-occupant strip, not a tab stack, because both Photoshop and Premiere ship exactly that.
dock_model.why_not_a_free_tile_tree_everywhere: egui_tiles gives free-form tiling but has no concept of edge affinity, icon-rail collapse, or a single-occupant contextual slot. Photoshop, Illustrator, Dreamweaver and Affinity all serialise EDGE-ANCHORED docks; Premiere serialises a pure splitter tree and is the outlier. Studio therefore owns the edge/rail/slot semantics and uses egui_tiles for the tiling INSIDE each region, which is where its tab and split behaviour is exactly right.

regions.name: Context Bar
regions.purpose: What the current tool and the current selection can do, right now. Never a tab stack.
regions.evidence: Photoshop declares anchor=top content=control-bar in 8 of 8 workspaces with panelid.static.options as the only occupant. Illustrator ships ControlBar in 12 of 12. InDesign ships 34 bound variants of one Control Panel. Affinity serialises a single tbar. No vendor with a workspace capture stacks tabs on the top edge.
regions.occupancy: Resolved by contextual_binding_rule against slot='context-bar'. The operator can pin an override; the pin is per document type.
regions.collapse: Hideable to 0px by a single toggle; never becomes an icon rail (there is nothing to enumerate).

regions.name: Tool Rail
regions.purpose: The tool palette. Outermost on the left, always visible.
regions.evidence: Premiere places Tools in a left rail in 18 of 19 placements. Photoshop declares anchor=left content='palette toolbar' in 8 of 8. Dreamweaver's Standard and Developer workspaces both declare a left panelframe of width=35 holding only DW_CodeView_Toolbar. Three independent vendors, same shape.
regions.occupancy: The tools panel. Its groups come from the document type. Affinity's tpnl proves the flyout-group serialisation.
regions.collapse: Single-column or double-column toggle. Cannot be emptied, can be moved to the right rail.

regions.name: Browse Dock
regions.purpose: What exists and what can be brought in. Sources, not properties.
regions.evidence: Premiere: Project LEFT 15/17, Media Browser LEFT 11/13, Effects browser LEFT 8/11, MarkerList LEFT 9/13. Affinity's left shelf, where present, holds assets, library, pages, presets and macros. Dreamweaver's Developer workspace docks site and snippets to a left panelframe of width=245.
regions.collapse: Collapses to a 32px ICON RAIL listing every registered panel of the dock, one icon each, with the active one highlighted. Clicking an icon opens the dock temporarily (overlay) or pins it open (shift-click). This is the mechanism that lets a task-episodic panel be reachable without being docked.

regions.name: Inspect Dock
regions.purpose: What is selected and how it is configured. The Properties slot is pinned to the top group.
regions.evidence: Premiere: Properties2 RIGHT 15/17, Search RIGHT 7/9, Color RIGHT 5/6, Essential Sound RIGHT 3/4. Affinity: 6 of 9 workspaces use exactly THREE right-shelf books. Photoshop's right dock is the palette home in 8 of 8. Illustrator Essentials leads AdobePropertiesPanel then AdobeLayerPalette - properties above layers.
regions.three_group_default_rationale: Affinity's modal answer is 3, and the three groups map cleanly onto three different refresh rhythms: group 1 changes with the SELECTION, group 2 with the OPERATOR's colour choices, group 3 with the DOCUMENT's structure. Putting panels with different refresh rhythms in the same stack is what makes a dock feel jumpy.
regions.collapse: Per-group collapse to a title strip, plus whole-dock collapse to a 32px icon rail.

regions.name: Meter Rail
regions.purpose: A continuously-updating readout that must never be hidden behind a tab.
regions.evidence: Premiere places MiniAudioMixer in a far-right narrow rail in 16 of 16 placements - the only 100 percent placement fact in the corpus.
regions.occupancy: audio-meters for video and motion; available to scopes on operator request. Hidden by default for non-temporal document types.

regions.name: Time & Results Dock
regions.purpose: Two things that are both wide and both about the whole document rather than the selection: TIME, and RESULTS.
regions.evidence: Premiere: Timeline CENTRE-BOTTOM 16/18. Photoshop declares anchor=bottom content=palette in 7 of 8 workspaces, occupied by the animation palette. Dreamweaver docks search, nodeOutput and DWGit to a bottom panelframe in both shipped workspaces.
regions.collapse: Collapses to a 28px icon rail. Auto-expands when a job writes a result into it (a preflight run, a find, a render) and returns to the rail when the operator dismisses. Auto-expand is per-panel opt-in and operator-disableable.

regions.name: Viewport
regions.purpose: The documents themselves. A clean, chrome-free surface holding an ARBITRARY number of editor groups, each with its own tab stack. The VS Code model, as required by OUI-002.

editor_group_model.rule: The centre is one egui_tiles Tree whose leaves are EDITOR GROUPS. A group is a tab stack of open documents and viewers. The number of groups is unbounded and never fixed - not two, not four, not 2x2.
editor_group_model.requirement_origin: OUI-002: 'any number of editor windows inside the one main window, each holding multiple tabs. It can be a single file with a chat beside it, or ten windows each with several tabs. The number must never be fixed.'
editor_group_model.defect_being_replaced: split_layout.rs's hard-coded 2x2 (pane-a..pane-d) with SplitWeights{vertical,horizontal}, which OUI-002 records was ported verbatim from app/src/App.tsx because the MT-006 acceptance criteria demanded those exact React field names. The module's own docstring already names egui_tiles as the intended engine for free-form docking. egui_tiles 0.14 with serde is already a dependency, so this is a microtask, not a rewrite.
editor_group_model.gestures: Drag a document tab onto another group's strip to move it; onto a group's body edge to split and create a new group; onto empty centre space to create a group. Close the last tab in a group and the group collapses, its space redistributed by egui_tiles. All four of these come from egui_tiles directly.
editor_group_model.mixed_content: A group's tabs may be documents, a source-viewer, a code view (reusing the existing code_editor module), or a RuntimeChat pane - which is what makes 'a single file with a chat beside it' a two-group centre rather than a special case.

regions.evidence: Premiere places Program Monitor CENTRE-TOP 16/19 and Timeline CENTRE-BOTTOM 16/18 - the centre is itself split when the document type needs two viewers. Photoshop's centre is a single canvas in all 8. Neither vendor fixes the count; Premiere's COLORANALYSIS workspace splits the centre three ways.
regions.occupancy: Document-type dependent DEFAULTS, not limits: raster/vector/photo = one group, one canvas; layout = one group plus an optional story/galley group; video/motion = one group split to program viewer and source-viewer; web = design view with an optional code-view group; photo-catalog = one group in grid, loupe, compare or survey mode.
regions.no_panels_rule: PANELS never dock into the centre; DOCUMENTS never dock into an edge. A panel dragged over the centre becomes a FLOATING panel, not a centre tile; a document tab dragged onto an edge is refused with a visible no-drop cue. This is the rule that keeps the viewport clean, which was an explicit operator requirement, and it is also what keeps the two egui_tiles tree families from having to share a tile type.

panel_states.description: A tab in a group of an edge dock. The normal state.
The visible tab of its group.
Registered in an edge but the edge is collapsed; reachable as an icon. Photoshop's anchor=none is_closed=true docks are the vendor precedent for this exact state.
Temporarily expanded over the viewport from an icon rail; closes on click-away. The state that makes task_episodic panels cheap.
A free window inside the Studio viewport bounds. Affinity's Retouching workspace ships 5 floating books, so this is a first-class state, not an edge case.
An OS window. The existing popout_window.rs already implements pop-out with merge-back and geometry clamping; Studio panels reuse it unchanged.
Registered but not reachable in the current layout; still enumerable through the panel picker.

reorganisation_gestures.gesture: drag tab onto another group's tab strip
reorganisation_gestures.result: move to that group at the drop index

reorganisation_gestures.gesture: drag tab onto a group's body edge
reorganisation_gestures.result: split that group, creating a new group in the same dock

reorganisation_gestures.gesture: drag tab onto a different EDGE
reorganisation_gestures.result: cross-dock move. Implemented as a PanelMoveRequest that removes the tile from the source edge's egui_tiles tree and inserts it into the target's; NOT an egui_tiles-internal drag, because the two trees are separate.

reorganisation_gestures.gesture: drag tab out of the window
reorganisation_gestures.result: pop out to an OS window via popout_window.rs
collapse the whole edge to its icon rail

reorganisation_gestures.gesture: click an icon in a collapsed rail
reorganisation_gestures.result: overlay; shift-click pins the edge open with that panel active
opens X in its default dock for the current document type, or focuses it if already open. Reuses the existing command_palette.rs and command_registry.rs.
a second instance with an independent parameter (e.g. preset-library filtered to gradients alongside one filtered to brushes). Required by the preset-library merge.

constraints: Minimum dock size is clamped exactly the way split_layout.rs already clamps dividers, so no dock can be dragged to zero and no panel can become unreachable.
An edge with zero panels renders as a 6px seam, not as nothing, so the operator can always drag a panel back to it.

Group count per EDGE is capped at 4. Premiere's deepest observed nesting inside one edge is 3 groups plus a rail; Affinity's is 3. A cap keeps the persisted tree small and the AccessKit tree shallow. This cap applies to edges ONLY - the centre editor tree is explicitly uncapped per OUI-002.

Every dock gesture, panel-open, panel-move and panel-close is a registered command in the existing command_registry.rs, so it is reachable from top_menu_bar.rs and command_palette.rs as well as by pointer. OUI-006 makes the menu the exhaustive index; a Studio surface that owns an action with no command is a defect.
The dock model must render correctly with all four edges absent, because OUI-009 embeds a Studio viewport inside Notes with no edge docks.

pointer_gesture_arbitration.why_this_is_here: OUI-008 makes every numeric field a press-and-drag scrub control. A dense panel is therefore a grid of drag targets sitting inside a drag-target tab, inside a drag-resizable dock, next to a pannable canvas. Four gesture consumers, one pointer. Leaving the arbitration to implementation guarantees the operator will one day drag a panel out of its dock while trying to nudge a value, so the rules are stated here.

rule_1_claim_at_press.rule: The topmost widget under the pointer at PRESS-DOWN claims the gesture for its entire duration. There is no movement threshold, no ambiguity window and no hand-off. A press inside a value field's body is owned by that field, full stop.
rule_1_claim_at_press.consequence: A drag beginning inside a field can never become a panel drag, a tab drag, a canvas pan, a dock resize, a marquee, or a scroll - regardless of direction, distance or speed.
rule_1_claim_at_press.egui_mechanics: The field body is a Sense::click_and_drag() region; egui assigns the interaction to it at press and holds it until release. No other widget may call ctx.set_dragged_id during an active gesture.

rule_2_drag_chrome_only.rule: Panel and tab drags may START ONLY from designated drag chrome: the tab itself, the group title strip, or the panel header. Never from the panel body.
rule_2_drag_chrome_only.why: This removes the conflict structurally rather than resolving it dynamically. It is also what every captured vendor does - a Photoshop, Illustrator or Premiere panel cannot be dragged by its body, only by its tab.
rule_2_drag_chrome_only.consequence: Rule 1 and rule 2 together mean the arbitration is decided by WHERE the press lands, which is inspectable and testable, rather than by gesture heuristics, which are not.

rule_3_splitters_are_separate_strips.rule: Dock splitters and group splitters are dedicated hit strips that never overlap a field body. Adopt split_layout.rs's existing constants: DIVIDER_THICKNESS 4.0 visual, DIVIDER_HIT_THICKNESS 8.0 interactive.
rule_3_splitters_are_separate_strips.cursor_disambiguation: OUI-008 requires a horizontal-resize cursor on a hovered scrub field so the control advertises itself. A dock splitter ALSO wants a resize cursor. They must NOT use the same icon or the operator cannot tell a value from a divider. Assignment: splitters use CursorIcon::ResizeHorizontal / ResizeVertical; scrub fields use CursorIcon::ResizeColumn (the double-arrow-with-bar form). If that reads too similarly in practice, the scrub field takes a custom cursor - but the two must remain visually distinct.
rule_3_splitters_are_separate_strips.spacing: A scrub field's hit rect is inset 8px from any splitter hit strip, so the last field in a panel cannot be mistaken for the dock edge.

rule_4_drag_leaves_the_panel.rule: Once a field owns the gesture, motion is tracked in SCREEN space, not panel-local space. The value keeps updating when the pointer leaves the field, leaves the panel, leaves the dock, crosses the canvas, crosses another panel, or leaves the application window entirely. Release anywhere commits.
rule_4_drag_leaves_the_panel.suppression_during_gesture: While a field owns the pointer: no other widget shows a hover state, no drop target activates, no tooltip fires, the panel's scroll area does not auto-scroll, the dock does not resize, and the canvas does not pan. The application is in a single captured-gesture state.
rule_4_drag_leaves_the_panel.escape_cancels: Escape during an active scrub aborts the gesture and restores the pre-press value. The undo transaction is discarded, not committed as a no-op.
rule_4_drag_leaves_the_panel.screen_edge: The value is NOT bounded by available screen travel. On reaching a screen edge the cursor is HIDDEN and delta continues to accumulate; the cursor is restored at the original press point on release. Deliberately NOT OS cursor warping: warping is fragile across multi-monitor Windows configurations and it moves a pointer the out-of-process inspector is tracking, which would corrupt GUI validation runs.
rule_4_drag_leaves_the_panel.clamping: Accumulated delta x step is clamped only to the parameter's real minimum and maximum, from the captured parameter metadata. Reaching a clamp shows a visual stop but does not end the gesture, so dragging back returns immediately rather than after re-traversing the overshoot.

rule_5_wheel.rule: The wheel over a hovered field steps that field's value, per OUI-008. The wheel elsewhere in the panel scrolls the panel.
rule_5_wheel.the_real_conflict: In a dense panel, most of the surface IS fields, so an unqualified 'wheel over field steps value' makes the panel nearly unscrollable by wheel. This is a genuine conflict, not a hypothetical: Illustrator's Transform panel is 240x298 and is almost entirely fields.
rule_5_wheel.mitigation: Every dense panel reserves a 10px SCROLL LANE on its inner right edge that contains no field and always takes the wheel, plus the wheel over any label, group header or blank area scrolls. That guarantees a wheel scroll target exists at every scroll position without qualifying the operator's stated behaviour.
rule_5_wheel.operator_preference: A preference inverts the default (wheel always scrolls; wheel-with-modifier steps the value). Recorded as OQ-12 rather than decided here.

rule_6_modifiers.proposal: Shift = coarse, step x10. Alt = fine, step x0.1. Shift+Alt = x0.01.
rule_6_modifiers.rationale: Matches Photoshop's own numeric-field convention. Alt is chosen for fine rather than Ctrl because Ctrl is a menu accelerator prefix and OUI-006 makes the menu load-bearing; and because Alt-drag-to-duplicate is a CANVAS gesture, so it cannot collide with a field gesture under rule 1.
rule_6_modifiers.modifier_ownership: Modifiers are sampled continuously during the gesture, not latched at press, so the operator can go coarse then fine within one drag. The step magnitude changes; the accumulated value does not jump.
rule_6_modifiers.status: The exact keys are listed in operator-ui-requirements.json open_for_operator_decision. Proposed here, not settled - see OQ-11.

rule_7_undo.rule: One undo entry per GESTURE. Press opens a transaction on the existing undo_stack.rs, all motion coalesces into it, release commits one entry naming the parameter and its before/after values.
rule_7_undo.wheel_coalescing: Consecutive wheel notches on the same field coalesce into one entry, closed by a 400ms idle timeout or by the pointer leaving the field.
rule_7_undo.accesskit_setvalue: A SetValue dispatched through AccessKit is one discrete entry and takes the identical clamp and commit path as the drag - never a separate code path, or the accessible value and the rendered value will drift.

rule_8_observability.requirement: The arbitration must be READABLE by the out-of-process inspector, not just correct. Expose studio.gesture.active as an AccessKit node whose value is the author_id of the widget currently owning the pointer, plus the gesture kind (scrub | tab-drag | panel-drag | splitter | pan | none).
rule_8_observability.why: Handshake validates GUI work out of process. A test asserting 'a drag from inside a field did not move the panel' needs to read WHO owned the gesture, not infer it from the absence of an effect. This one node makes every rule above directly testable.

panel_density_model.why_this_is_here: OUI-008 makes panel density a sizing constraint rather than a style choice. A scrub field needs a grabbable body, so the number of parameters a docked panel can carry at a given width is bounded, and the dock widths proposed above have to be justified against that bound rather than picked.
panel_density_model.vendor_anchor: Illustrator declares a preferred docked size for 49 surfaces in its own workspace file. Median width 240, mode 240 (30 of 49). Character 240x188, Transform 240x298, Align 244x172, Pathfinder 240x107, Stroke 240x31. 240px is therefore the field-tested floor for a dense parameter panel - measured from the capture, not estimated.

scrub_allowance.field_body_minimum: 72px wide x 24px tall. 24px is the practical minimum pointer target for a press-and-drag grab; a vendor-era 20px row is fine for click-to-type but too thin to grab reliably.
scrub_allowance.width_delta: A vendor field body is roughly 56px. The scrub minimum adds about 16px per field. A two-field row (X/Y, W/H) adds about 32px.
scrub_allowance.derived_floor: 240 vendor floor + 32 scrub allowance = 272. Rounded up for a scrollbar gutter and the 10px scroll lane: 300px.

dock_width_budget.content_width_at_300: 300 - 12 left padding - 12 right padding - 10 scroll lane = 266px usable.
dock_width_budget.rows_that_fit: One labelled scalar per row (label 96 + gap 8 + field 72 = 176, fits with slack), OR one label plus two linked scalars (label 24 + field 72 + gap 8 + field 72 = 176, fits), which is how X/Y and W/H pairs are laid out. THREE fields on one row does not fit at 300px and must not be attempted.
dock_width_budget.vertical_budget: A right group at 34 percent of a 900px column is 306px; minus a 26px tab strip and 8px padding leaves 272px, which is about 9 rows. Cross-check: Illustrator's own Transform panel preferred height is 298px, which at 28px pitch is about 10 rows. The budget and the vendor's own declared height agree, which is the reassurance that 300x300 is a realistic group, not an optimistic one.
dock_width_budget.below_minimum_behaviour: Below 260px the panel switches to a stacked compact form - label above field, one field per row, 20px pitch, click-to-type still available but the drag target reduced. The panel does not clip and does not hide controls; it changes layout. A panel that would clip instead shows a horizontal scroll, never a truncated field.

wide_format_rule.rule: A panel declaring preferred_width greater than 320 is registered in its edge but presents as an OVERLAY or FLOATING panel by default rather than occupying a dock tab.
wide_format_rule.evidence: Eight Illustrator surfaces exceed 320px: AdobeAltGlyphsPanel 404, AdobeHorizontalTabPanel 430, AdobeFlatteningPreview 490, Stock Unified Content 400, CCX Commenting 350, PatternOptions 288 (borderline), Export 270 (borderline). The vendor does not force these into its own 240 dock.
wide_format_rule.consequence_for_the_defaults_above: library appears in several default left docks. At 260px it renders its compact list form; its grid form is an overlay. tabs-indents is already assigned to the top strip, which is the one region wide enough for a 430px ruler. glyphs is task_episodic and reached from the rail, never a default dock tab.

panels_reclassified_by_density.note: Density changes which panels can share a group, because a group's height is divided among its tabs' content, and a field-dense panel wastes the space a list-dense panel would use.
panels_reclassified_by_density.rule: Do not stack a FIELD-DENSE panel (transform, character, paragraph, effect-controls, adjustments, stroke) in the same group as a LIST-DENSE panel (layers, swatches, library, project-bin) when the group is under 300px tall. Field-dense panels want a fixed modest height; list-dense panels want all the height they can get, and a shared group forces one of them to be wrong.
audit_of_the_proposed_defaults: raster group 3 [layers, channels, paths, history] - all list-dense, 46 percent height. Correct.
raster group 1 [properties, adjustments, effect-controls, masks] - all field-dense, 30 percent. Correct.

vector group 2 [colour, swatches, align-distribute, pathfinder, navigator, info] - MIXED. swatches is list-dense, align-distribute and pathfinder are button grids, colour is field-dense. At 24 percent of 900px = 216px this group is tight for swatches. Accepted because Illustrator's own preferred heights for these are all small - Swatches 111, Pathfinder 107, Align 172, Info 88 - so 216px is above every one of them.

layout group 1 [properties, character, paragraph, text-frame, text-wrap, opentype] - six field-dense panels at 34 percent = 306px. Character 188 and Paragraph 257 both fit; text-frame will scroll. Accepted, with text-frame ordered last.

photo group 2 [adjustments, effect-controls, properties, masks] at 52 percent = 468px - the largest field-dense allocation in any layout, which is correct because a develop stack is the tallest field grid in the product.

shared_rules: Every layout has the Context Bar on top and the Tool Rail on the left. No exceptions - this is 8/8 Photoshop, 12/12 Illustrator, 18/19 Premiere.
The FIRST tab of the FIRST right group is always the Properties slot. 15/17 Premiere and the Illustrator Essentials / Photoshop Assisted ordering.
The LAST right group is always the document structure group, and layers is its first tab. Photoshop's own trailing group order is layers, channels, paths in 4 of 8 workspaces.
Panels listed after a '|' are tabs in the same group, in that tab order, with the first one active.
Panels listed under icon_rail are registered in that edge but the edge starts collapsed.

raster.derived_from: Photoshop Photography + Painting workspaces; Affinity Pixel workspace (3 right books, 1 left book)
justification: Group 3 tab order layers|channels|paths is Photoshop's own trailing group order, identical in Graphic and Web, Painting, Photography and Motion.

Group 2 groups picker+swatches with the histogram: Photoshop places picker, swatches, gradients, patterns consecutively, and Affinity's Pixel right-shelf book 1 is exactly histogram, scopes, colour, swatches.

Group 1 leads with the contextual slot then the two panels that edit the selected layer's non-destructive stack. Affinity's Pixel book 2 leads with adjustments then metadata then layers, which is the same idea with a different split point.

The left dock starts collapsed because Photoshop ships NO left browse dock at all - only the toolbar - and Affinity's Pixel workspace is the only pixel-side workspace with a left shelf. Collapsed-but-registered is the honest compromise between the two vendors.
Timeline is registered in the bottom rail but collapsed: Photoshop declares a bottom palette dock in 7 of 8 workspaces but only Motion and Core Tools open the animation palette.

vector.derived_from: Illustrator Essentials Classic and Painting workspaces; Affinity Vector workspace (3 right books, empty left shelf)
justification: Group 1 is Illustrator's Painting lead sequence with Transparency folded into Appearance: Appearance, NamedStyle, Gradient, Transparency are consecutive there, and AdobePropertiesPanel leads Essentials.

Transform + Align + Pathfinder are consecutive in 5 of 12 Illustrator workspaces; align-distribute and pathfinder therefore share a group, with transform promoted into group 1 because it is selection-driven.

Artboards sits with layers because Illustrator's Printing and Proofing workspace orders Artboards immediately after AdobeLayerPalette, and Essentials Classic orders AdobeLayerPalette, Export, Artboards.
Affinity's Vector workspace has an EMPTY left shelf. The left dock therefore starts collapsed, matching both vendors.

layout.derived_from: Illustrator Layout and Typography workspaces; Affinity Layout workspace (left shelf with 6 visible, 3 right books); InDesign panel plugin inventory
justification: The left dock is EXPANDED here and collapsed for raster/vector because Affinity's Layout workspace is one of only six with a populated left shelf, and its visible left entries are the page/long-document/preflight family. Illustrator's Layout workspace also promotes Links and Export into its lead group.

Group 1's typography run is Illustrator Typography's exact lead order: Character, Paragraph, AdobeOpenTypeFont, AdobeCharStyles, AdobeParaStyles - with the styles pair split into group 2 because styles are chosen less often than character attributes are nudged.
The bottom dock is EXPANDED because preflight is a continuous concern in a layout document. InDesign devotes 39 captured surfaces to Package and Preflight UI, more than any other single plugin.

motion.derived_from: Premiere EFFECTS and COLOR workspaces (dvaui, the same engine After Effects uses); Photoshop Motion workspace
motion.coverage_caveat: EXTRAPOLATED. No After Effects workspace file was captured. See coverage_gaps.
motion.centre: composition viewer (egui_tiles tree; splits to composition + source-viewer on demand)
justification: effect-controls takes the largest right group and leads group 1 because in a motion document the keyframe stack IS the work. Premiere's own legacy placement co-tabs Effect Controls with the Source Monitor (LEFT 5, CENTRE-TOP 4), but its modern Properties2 placement is right, and a keyframe editor needs height, which the right dock has and the centre-top stack does not.
Timeline at 300px is the tallest bottom dock of any type: Premiere's Timeline occupies roughly the lower 42 percent of the frame in the EDITING and PRODUCTION workspaces.
Meter rail visible: Premiere shows MiniAudioMixer in every workspace that has audio.

video.derived_from: Premiere EDITING workspace, which is the vendor's own default for this document type
video.centre: egui_tiles horizontal split: source-viewer left, program viewer right
justification: This is a near-direct transcription of Premiere's EDITING workspace: Source Monitor + Effect Controls + AudioClipMixer + MetadataEditor top-left; Program Monitor top-centre; Properties2 + Search top-right; Project + Media Browser + Graphics + Libraries + Info + Effects + MarkerList + History lower-left; Tools rail; Timeline lower-centre; MiniAudioMixer far-right rail.

Two right groups rather than three: the EDITING workspace has a single tall right pane holding Properties2, Search and UXP. Video is the one document type where Affinity's three-book modal answer does not apply, because Premiere is the vendor of record for it.
The centre is split rather than stacked because Premiere's Program and Source monitors are side-by-side in 8 of the workspaces containing both.

web.derived_from: Dreamweaver Standard and Developer workspaces; Illustrator Web workspace
web.centre: egui_tiles vertical split: design view top, code view bottom (code view reuses the existing code_editor module). Split ratio 1.0 (design only) in Standard, 0.0 (code only) in a Developer preset.
justification: Left width 245 is Dreamweaver's own Developer panelframe width, read from the capture.

Dreamweaver's Standard workspace docks site, CC Libraries, objects (Insert), assets, snippets, CSS Designer and DOM to the RIGHT, but its Developer workspace docks site and snippets LEFT. Studio follows Developer's split - sources left, inspectors right - because that is consistent with all four other vendors, and Standard's right-side pile-up is a Dreamweaver idiosyncrasy that puts the file tree and the CSS inspector in the same column.
Bottom holds Dreamweaver's own bottom panelframe contents: search, nodeOutput and DWGit, mapped to find-replace, problems and the existing SourceControl shell pane.

photo.derived_from: Lightroom Classic develop parameters and catalog model; Affinity Retouching and Colour Grading workspaces
photo.coverage_caveat: EXTRAPOLATED for the catalog side. No Lightroom Classic panel layout was captured.
photo.centre: photo viewport with a mode selector: grid | loupe | compare | survey. Mode lives in the centre, NOT in a persona.
justification: Scopes on TOP of the right column, alone in a short group: this is the one layout where the histogram outranks everything, and it is the only placement all three photo-adjacent sources agree on (Lightroom's histogram is the top-right element; Affinity's Colour Grading and Retouching workspaces both open with a scope-bearing right book; Photoshop's Photography workspace opens histogram).

adjustments gets 52 percent of the right column because for a photo document the adjustment stack IS the document. Lightroom's develop parameter capture is the largest single parameter surface among the non-Adobe-dvaui apps.
Affinity's Retouching workspace is the only one of nine that floats five separate books. That is a symptom of a right column too small for the job, and the 52 percent allocation is the direct fix.

cross_type_table.note: Panels present in every default layout: context-bar, tools, properties, layers, colour, swatches, history, info. Eight panels form the invariant spine. Everything else varies by type - which is what makes the doc-type default meaningful rather than cosmetic.

contextual_binding_rule.origin: A direct generalisation of Dreamweaver's property inspector API as captured in dreamweaver_panels_dialogs.json: 60 of 60 inspectors declare {tag, attrname, priority, selection, hideclass} and implement canInspectSelection / inspectSelection / initializeUI / displayHelp. Corroborated by InDesign's 34 Control Panel resource variants and 14 Alignment Panel variants, and by Premiere's Properties2 slot.

what_a_panel_declares.author_id: string, stable, kebab-case, globally unique. The AccessKit identity as well as the registry key.
what_a_panel_declares.slot: one of: context-bar | inspector | free. 'free' panels are never auto-resolved; they are placed by the layout and only their ENABLEMENT is contextual.
what_a_panel_declares.binds_to: array of selector strings. Grammar: 'node:<PrimitiveName>' (vocabulary from the capability registry's document_primitives: Document, TextNode, VectorNode, FrameNode, ComponentNode, InstanceNode, RectangleNode, BooleanOperationNode, ...), 'tag:<htmlTag>' for web documents (Dreamweaver's tag values verbatim, including alternation 'input|div' and pseudo-tags '*LOCKED*', '*COMMENT*'), 'track:<audio|video|caption>' for temporal documents, 'tool:<toolId>' for tool-driven binding, 'document' for the no-selection case, and '*' as the wildcard.
what_a_panel_declares.attr_match: optional {key, op, value}. Dreamweaver's attrname, generalised from presence-only to a comparison. Example from the capture: OAWidget.htm binds tag='*' with attrname='OAWidgetID' at priority 5 - a wildcard tag rescued to usefulness by an attribute test.
what_a_panel_declares.selection_scope: one of: exact | within | ancestor | multiple | none. exact and within are Dreamweaver's own values (33 and 25 of 60 respectively). insideLock, which Dreamweaver uses once, generalises to 'ancestor' with a lock predicate. 'multiple' and 'none' are Studio additions for cases Dreamweaver's single-selection model never had.
what_a_panel_declares.priority: integer. HIGHER WINS. Semantics proven inside the capture, not assumed: spry_widget.htm binds tag=div at 1 as the catch-all while six widget inspectors bind tag=div at 50; meta.htm binds META at 5 while its four refined siblings bind META at 6. Studio adopts Dreamweaver's observed bands verbatim so a port is mechanical: 1 = catch-all fallback, 5 = concrete primitive, 6 = refined primitive variant, 10 = template or structural construct, 50 = named component or widget instance.
what_a_panel_declares.document_types: array. A hard pre-filter; a panel not declared for the active document type never enters resolution.
what_a_panel_declares.can_bind: runtime predicate, the port of canInspectSelection. Implemented by every one of the 60 captured inspectors, so it is not optional. It may VETO regardless of priority, which is what lets a high-priority binding decline a selection it cannot actually edit.
what_a_panel_declares.hide_when_unbound: boolean, the port of hideclass. If true the panel disappears from its stack when unbound; if false it renders an explanatory empty state. Default false, because a tab that vanishes breaks muscle memory and breaks an agent's ability to address it.

resolution_algorithm: 1. PRE-FILTER by document_types against the active document. Panels outside the type are not candidates.

2. MATCH binds_to against the selection, honouring selection_scope: exact matches the selected node's own primitive; within matches any ancestor of the caret or selection; ancestor matches the nearest enclosing container only; multiple applies only when the selection count is greater than one, resolving to the nearest common supertype for a heterogeneous selection; none matches with no selection at all.
3. APPLY attr_match. A declared attr_match that fails removes the candidate even if the tag matched.
4. CALL can_bind(selection). A false is an absolute veto and is applied BEFORE priority so a high-priority binding cannot squat on a selection it cannot edit.

6. TIE-BREAK deterministically, in this order: (a) narrower selection_scope wins - exact over within over ancestor; (b) concrete binds_to over alternation over wildcard; (c) attr_match present over absent; (d) lexicographic author_id. Step (d) exists solely so the resolution is byte-stable frame to frame, because the AccessKit tree must be deterministic for the out-of-process inspector.

7. FILL THE SLOT. For slot='context-bar' (single-occupant): rank 1 only. For slot='inspector': rank 1 becomes the ACTIVE tab of the properties group; ranks 2..5 become sibling tabs in the same group, in rank order. Capping at 5 total is a judgement call - Premiere's deepest single group is 13 tabs, but 13 auto-generated tabs would be unreadable.

8. NO-SELECTION FALLBACK. When nothing is selected, resolve against binds_to='document' with selection_scope='none'. There is always at least one such binding (Document Setup), so the inspector is never blank. Dreamweaver has no equivalent and shows an empty inspector, which is a defect to fix rather than copy.
anti_thrash_rules: STICKY ACTIVE TAB: when the operator manually activates a non-rank-1 tab in the inspector group, that choice is remembered keyed by (document_type, resolved primitive). Selecting another node of the same primitive re-activates the operator's choice, not rank 1. Selecting a node of a different primitive re-runs resolution. Without this, an inspector that re-resolves on every click is actively hostile.
RESOLUTION HYSTERESIS: resolution runs on selection CHANGE, not per frame. A drag that momentarily passes through a different selection state does not re-resolve until the drag ends.
STABLE TAB SET: ranks 2..5 are recomputed only when rank 1 changes. Otherwise the sibling tabs stay put, so a tab does not move under the pointer.
why_this_replaces_the_persona_toggle: A persona swaps every tool, every panel and the whole context bar at once, on an explicit operator action, for the whole application. Its cost is visible in the capture: Affinity's Slice workspace exists to show what amounts to one export panel, and its Typography workspace ships five books of one entry each.

This model instead: (1) the DOCUMENT TYPE picks the default layout once, at open, and never again; (2) the SELECTION picks the contents of two slots continuously and silently; (3) a TASK brings its episodic panel in as an overlay and lets it leave. Nothing ever swaps wholesale, the operator's own arrangement is never destroyed by a mode change, and there is no toggle to hunt for.
The operator's own words - 'panels to be job-related and contextual instead of the whole interface switching' - map exactly onto (2) and (3).

worked_examples.selection: a text frame in a layout document, caret inside the text
worked_examples.context_bar_resolves_to: character-attributes bar (binds_to node:TextNode, scope exact, priority 5)
worked_examples.note: character wins over text-frame because scope=exact beats scope=ancestor at equal priority.

worked_examples.selection: the same text frame selected as an object, no caret
worked_examples.note: Same object, different scope, different resolution. This is the behaviour InDesign implements with 34 Control Panel variants.
Dreamweaver has no multiple scope; this is the Studio addition.

worked_examples.selection: an audio clip on a video timeline
worked_examples.inspector_group_becomes: [effect-controls* with the audio-role section, properties, metadata]
worked_examples.note: Premiere's Essential Sound is this resolution, not a separate panel.

persistence_model.verdict: Layout is PER DOCUMENT TYPE, with a per-tab override layer and a named-preset layer. NOT per project.
reasoning: Per project is wrong: it means every new project starts from the shipped default and the operator re-arranges forever. The vendors agree - Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere and Affinity all scope workspaces to the APPLICATION, never to the document. Not one of the 50 captured workspace files is project-scoped.

Per document type is right because the arrangement is a property of the JOB, and the job is what the document type encodes. A second raster file must look identical to the first or muscle memory is worthless.

A per-tab override layer is nevertheless required, because the operator explicitly opens multiple tabs for different files at once and may want one of them in a comparison or reference arrangement without contaminating the type default.

layers.name: named_preset
layers.content: operator-saved named arrangements within a type, e.g. 'Retouch' or 'Colour pass' for raster. The vendor 'workspace' concept, but scoped to a type so it can never swap the whole application.
layers.selector: a small dropdown in the Studio tab strip, listing only presets for the active type.

layers.name: user_default
layers.content: the operator's live arrangement for this type. Written automatically, debounced, whenever the operator moves anything. This is the layer that makes rearrangement stick.

layers.name: tab_override
layers.content: a diff against L2 for one open document tab. Created only when the operator changes the layout while a per-tab override is explicitly engaged (a lock icon in the tab). Ephemeral by default; promoted to durable only if that tab is part of a saved session.

persistence_model.resolution: effective_layout = L3 ?? (selected L1 preset) ?? L2 ?? L0, keyed by document_type.

L1_and_L2.why: These are OPERATOR preferences, not workspace state. The existing workbench layout endpoint is /workspaces/:workspace_id/workbench/layout, i.e. per workspace, which is the wrong scope for a per-operator per-document-type arrangement. preference_client.rs already exists in the shell and is the correct home.
L1_and_L2.risk_flagged: If preference_client.rs turns out to be workspace-scoped too, this needs an operator-scoped key namespace before Studio ships. Listed in open_questions.

L3.how: Add a `studio` object to the native snapshot under LAYOUT_SCHEMA_ID hsk.native_worksurface_layout@1, or ship a sibling schema hsk.studio_dock_layout@1 through the same PUT /workspaces/:workspace_id/workbench/layout endpoint. The backend already stores layout_state as opaque JSON and distinguishes payloads by schema_id - that is exactly how the native and React schemas already coexist in one column. A sibling schema is preferred: it keeps the Studio blob independently versionable and lets a Studio schema bump not invalidate the shell layout.
L3.validation: Reuse LayoutSnapshot::validate's discipline: a structurally-corrupt-but-schema-valid Studio blob must be rejected and fall back to last-known-good, then to L2, then to L0. A Studio blob referencing a panel author_id that no longer exists drops that panel and logs, rather than failing the whole restore.

multi_tab_behaviour: Opening a second document of the SAME type in a new Studio tab: identical layout, shared L2. Moving a panel in either tab moves it in both, because they share the layer.

Opening a document of a DIFFERENT type in a new Studio tab: the layout changes when that tab is activated. This is the one place Studio does change the whole panel arrangement - and it is triggered by opening a different kind of document, not by a mode toggle. That distinction is the whole design.
The transition is animated and reversible, and the outgoing type's arrangement is preserved untouched, which is precisely what a persona toggle does not do.

Panels that exist in both types (the eight-panel invariant spine) keep their edge and group index across the switch wherever the target layout also places them there, so the switch does not feel like a reset.

what_exists_today.fact: PaneId = Arc<str>, BTreeMap-keyed for deterministic iteration, monotonic AccessKit NodeId counter starting at PANE_NODE_ID_BASE = 100, author_id is the kebab-case pane_id. PaneRecord carries pane_id, pane_type, project_id, content_id, lock_state, dirty, authority. PaneFactory is a trait with pane_type/render/accesskit role.
what_exists_today.studio_impact: Studio's panel registry MIRRORS these conventions rather than reusing PaneRecord, because a Studio panel is not a shell pane: it has a dock, a group, a tab index, a binding declaration and an optional instance parameter, none of which PaneRecord models. A parallel StudioPanelRegistry with the same Arc<str> + BTreeMap + stable-author_id discipline is the right shape.

what_exists_today.fact: A hand-rolled 2x2 (pane-a..pane-d) with SplitWeights{vertical,horizontal}, SPLIT_MIN 0.2 / SPLIT_MAX 0.8 / SPLIT_STEP 0.05, dividers as Role::Splitter with author_ids divider-horizontal (NodeId 30) and divider-vertical (31) and a clamped SetValue action. Its own module doc already states: 'egui_tiles remains the intended engine for free-form docking work where its tree model is the right tool.'
what_exists_today.studio_impact: OUI-002 settles this: the fixed 2x2 is a recorded DEFECT, it exists only because the MT-006 acceptance criteria demanded the old React field names verbatim, and replacing it with the tile tree is a microtask. Studio's centre editor tree therefore REPLACES split_layout.rs's role rather than sitting beside it. Recommended sequencing: Studio builds the unbounded centre tree first and proves it; the shell's remaining split_layout.rs callers migrate onto that same tree in a follow-on microtask; split_layout.rs is deleted only when its last caller is gone. What survives from it permanently is its clamp discipline (clamp_split, apply_set_value, SPLIT_MIN/MAX/STEP, DIVIDER_THICKNESS 4.0 and DIVIDER_HIT_THICKNESS 8.0) and its Role::Splitter + clamped SetValue convention, all of which Studio's dock dividers adopt unchanged - including the hit-thickness constant, which pointer_gesture_arbitration rule 3 depends on.

what_exists_today.fact: TabBarState{tabs, active_index} with TabState{pane_type, content_id, pinned, dirty}, cross-pane drag via TabDragPayload/TabDropTarget/apply_drop, tab-bar containers at fixed NodeIds 60..63, individual tabs addressed by hashed egui::Id derived from the author_id string tab-{pane_id}-{index}.
what_exists_today.studio_impact: Studio's DOCUMENT tabs (the multiple files and projects the operator opens inside the module) reuse this directly. Studio's PANEL tabs need a separate widget because TabState is keyed to PaneType and a panel tab needs a panel author_id plus an instance parameter. The drag/drop contract (TabDragPayload/TabDropTarget/apply_drop) is the right shape to generalise for cross-DOCK moves and should be lifted to a shared trait rather than duplicated. IMPROVEMENT TO ADOPT: tab_bar.rs addresses tabs by INDEX (tab-{pane}-{index}), which shifts under reorder; Studio panel tabs should be addressed by NAME instead.

what_exists_today.fact: An egui::SidePanel::left('left-rail') with a 32px always-visible activity icon strip plus an expandable 220px panel, collapse state persisted to drawers.project, fixed AccessKit NodeIds 80..88.
what_exists_today.studio_impact: COLLISION: the shell already owns the left edge. Studio's Tool Rail cannot be the outermost left element without displacing it. Proposal: when ModuleId::Studio is active the shell's left_rail auto-collapses to its 32px icon strip (a capability it already has) and Studio's Tool Rail renders immediately inboard of it, giving 44 + 32 = 76px of left chrome before the Browse Dock. Flagged as a tradeoff, not a settled answer.

what_exists_today.fact: MODULE_DEFINITIONS is a compile-time [ModuleDefinition; 6]. The STUDIO entry currently declares tabs [ModelRuntime, Swarm, InferenceLab, FontManager, KernelDcc, UserManual] with default_tab ModelRuntime - byte-identical in intent to the LAB entry. Studio is a placeholder in the shell today.
what_exists_today.studio_impact: This entry MUST be rewritten as part of Studio. It also carries a constraint the proposal must respect: module_tab_list() rewrites the active pane's tab list on module switch as uniqueTabs([default, ...module.tabs, ...existing]). Studio's document tabs are documents, not PaneTypes, so Studio needs either a new PaneType::StudioDocument(String) variant or an escape from the MODULE_DEFINITIONS tab model. Recommend a single PaneType::StudioViewport whose content_id is the document id, so the existing tab machinery keeps working unchanged.

what_exists_today.fact: LAYOUT_SCHEMA_ID hsk.native_worksurface_layout@1, LAYOUT_SNAPSHOT_VERSION 1, persisted via PUT /workspaces/:workspace_id/workbench/layout as an opaque layout_state JSON with an EventLedger event id. SurrealDB-authoritative, no local file. LayoutTransport abstracts the send for testability. Restore validates and falls back to last-known-good then default.
what_exists_today.studio_impact: Reused as described in persistence_model. The schema_id discrimination pattern is already proven by the native and React schemas sharing one column.

what_exists_today.fact: egui 0.33, eframe 0.33 with features wgpu + accesskit + persistence, egui_tiles 0.14 with serde, egui_kittest 0.33 with wgpu + eframe.
what_exists_today.studio_impact: Everything Studio needs is already a dependency. egui_tiles' serde feature is what makes per-region tree persistence cheap. egui_kittest is the harness the GUI validation runs through.

egui_tiles_usage.one_tree_per_region: Five independent egui_tiles::Tree instances: left, right, bottom, centre, and (only when a dock is split into groups) the group container inside each. Not one global tree.
egui_tiles_usage.why_not_one_tree: A single tree cannot express 'this tile is anchored to the right edge and collapses to an icon rail', and a stray drag could dissolve the edge structure entirely. Separate trees make the edge semantics structural rather than conventional.
egui_tiles_usage.cross_tree_moves: A drag from one edge to another is a Handshake-level PanelMoveRequest: remove the tile from the source Tree, insert into the target Tree at the drop index. egui_tiles supports both halves; what it does not supply is the edge-aware drop targeting, which Studio draws itself.
egui_tiles_usage.what_egui_tiles_supplies: Tab strips, tab drag within and between containers of the same tree, splitters with drag resize, serde round-trip of the tile tree. That is the majority of the work.
egui_tiles_usage.what_studio_supplies: Edge anchoring, icon-rail collapse, single-occupant slots, contextual resolution, the panel registry, AccessKit identity, and the persistence cascade.

shell_integration.module_boundary: Studio is a MODULE inside the Handshake shell, not a second shell. Above Studio: the shell title bar, the shell left_rail (collapsed), the module switcher, the project tabs. Inside Studio: its own document tab strip (reusing tab_bar.rs), then the five-region dock model. The shell's status bar stays at the bottom of the window, below Studio's bottom dock.
migration_sequence_suggested: 2. Unbounded centre editor tree over egui_tiles, replacing the fixed 2x2 for Studio (OUI-002). Prove N groups with tabs, cross-group document drag, and serde round-trip.

3. The scrub value control as ONE widget with its clamp-and-commit path, its AccessKit SpinButton contract, and its gesture capture. Built before any dense panel, because every dense panel depends on it and because pointer_gesture_arbitration is only testable once it exists.
4. StudioPanelRegistry + binding declarations for a spine of 8 panels only.
5. Five-region dock host with the right dock functional and the other three stubbed; adopt split_layout.rs's clamp and hit-thickness constants for the dividers.
6. Contextual resolution for slot='inspector' with three bindings, proven end to end through the AccessKit inspector before adding more.
7. The remaining 66 panels as content work behind a stable registry API, fed by captured parameter metadata.

Rationale: the risk in this design is concentrated in three places - the centre tree, the scrub widget and the resolver - and none of it is in the panels. Steps 2, 3 and 6 are the ones worth proving with a deliberately small panel set. Step 3 is placed before the docks because a scrub control retrofitted into finished panels would have to re-litigate every gesture boundary.

accessibility_scheme.principle: Every Studio surface is addressable by a stable, name-based author_id that survives reorder, collapse, theme change and restart. The out-of-process inspector must be able to answer 'what is on screen, where, and what did the binding rule decide' from the AccessKit tree alone, with no screen reading and no guessing.
accessibility_scheme.convention: studio.<kind>.<region>[.<name>][#<instance>] - all lowercase, dot-separated, kebab-case within a segment. Matches the existing shell convention (left-rail.activity.files, module-main, divider-horizontal, tab-{pane}-{index}) while being unambiguously namespaced.

id_grammar.note: n is the group's ordinal in the centre tile tree, 1-based in tree traversal order. Unbounded count per OUI-002.
One strip per editor group, not one for the module.
Named by DOCUMENT, not by group and not by index, so moving a document between editor groups does not change its address. Fixes the reorder instability in tab_bar.rs's tab-{pane}-{index}.
