Present whenever the panel is registered in that edge, whether the edge is collapsed or not, so an agent can always open a panel by one stable id.
n is the group's ordinal within the dock, 1-based, top to bottom or left to right.
NAME-based, not index-based. Reordering tabs changes their position but not their id.
Second and later instances only. The first instance carries no suffix, so existing addresses never change when a second is opened.
SetValue clamped exactly as split_layout.rs::apply_set_value clamps, so an agent cannot collapse a dock to zero.

id_grammar.value: the author_id of the panel the binding rule chose, plus the matched selector and the winning priority, as a compact string
id_grammar.note: THE key observability affordance. Without it an agent must infer the resolver's decision from what happens to be visible; with it, one read gives the decision, the input and the reason.
Every scrubbable numeric control per OUI-008. See value_field_contract below.

id_grammar.value: the author_id of the widget currently owning the pointer plus the gesture kind (scrub | tab-drag | panel-drag | splitter | pan | none)
id_grammar.note: Makes pointer_gesture_arbitration directly testable out of process rather than inferable from side effects.

id_grammar.value: a JSON projection of the whole dock model - regions, groups, tab order, active tabs, collapse states, floating and popped-out panels, plus the centre editor tree
id_grammar.note: One read yields the entire layout. Grounded in the existing UiTreeSnapshot::to_json pattern in accessibility/snapshot.rs. This is what makes a GUI regression test a string comparison rather than a screenshot diff.

value_field_contract.requirement_origin: OUI-008, whose accessibility_requirement states that the same clamped set-value path must be reachable through AccessKit and that the accessible value, minimum, maximum and unit must agree with what the control renders.
value_field_contract.role: accesskit::Role::SpinButton for a bounded scalar; Role::Slider where the parameter's captured metadata declares a slider range distinct from its edit range (Illustrator's EVE sources carry exactly that distinction across 2109 parameters).
required_properties: value (the formatted string exactly as rendered, including unit and decimal places)
value_field_contract.single_path_rule: SetValue, Increment, Decrement, wheel, drag and typed entry all converge on ONE clamp-and-commit function. If any of them has its own clamp, the accessible value and the rendered value will eventually disagree, which is exactly the failure the out-of-process inspector exists to catch and would then be unable to catch.
value_field_contract.metadata_source: min, max, step, unit and decimal precision are read from the captured parameter metadata rather than hand-configured - Illustrator EVE (2109 parameters across 559 layouts), Photoshop type-library help strings (35 ranges, 140 defaults, 43 units), Premiere Lumetri (98 parameters with hard bounds separate from UI bounds), Affinity brush schema (observed min/max). A parameter with no captured metadata renders as unbounded with a logged warning, never as a silently invented range.
value_field_contract.undo_visibility: Each committed gesture emits one undo entry whose label names the parameter and its before and after values, so an agent reading the undo stack can verify a scrub did what it intended without re-reading the field.
value_field_contract.density_interaction: The field's AccessKit bounds must be its GRAB rect (72x24 minimum), not its glyph rect. An inspector computing a click point from the reported bounds must land inside the draggable body.

id_space_registration: Studio panel counts are DYNAMIC, so Studio must NOT consume the small fixed NodeId band (10, 20, 21, 30, 31, 40..43, 50, 51..56, 60..67, 80..90, panes at 100+). It follows the tab_bar.rs precedent instead: derive egui::Id from the author_id STRING via egui::Id::new, landing in egui's hashed space, which is disjoint from the small fixed band by construction.

Register the prefix 'studio.' in accessibility::registry::DECLARED_HASHED_AUTHOR_ID_PREFIXES so the existing collision test and the assert_no_unnamed_interactive check cover every Studio node without enumerating them.
The five REGION containers are fixed in count and may take fixed NodeIds if a fresh band is wanted; recommend NOT doing so, to keep one rule for the whole module.
determinism_requirements: Panel iteration order is BTreeMap order on author_id, mirroring pane_registry.rs, so the emitted tree is byte-identical frame to frame for an unchanged layout.
Contextual resolution runs on selection change only, and its tie-break terminates in a lexicographic author_id comparison, so the same selection always yields the same tree.
A panel in state 'collapsed_to_rail' still emits its studio.rail.<region>.<panel> node. An agent must never have to expand a dock to discover that a panel exists.
hide_when_unbound defaults to false precisely so a contextual panel's node does not vanish from the tree; it renders an empty state with bound=false instead.
agent_steerability_contract: Open a panel: dispatch Click on studio.rail.<region>.<panel>, or the command-palette command, whichever the caller prefers. Both must exist.
Read the layout: read the value of studio.dock.state.
Read what the resolver decided: read studio.slot.inspector.resolved.
Resize a dock: SetValue on studio.split.<region>.<n>, clamped.

Move a panel: not directly steerable by a single AccessKit action; expose an explicit command 'studio.move-panel' taking {panel, region, group, index} through the existing command_registry.rs rather than trying to synthesise a drag. Synthesising drags out of process is fragile and should not be the supported path.

Set a value: SetValue on studio.field.<panel>.<parameter>, clamped by the same function the drag uses. Increment and Decrement step by numeric_value_step. NEVER synthesise a scrub drag out of process - it is the one gesture whose correctness depends on continuous screen-space delta and it would be untestable.

Verify a gesture did not leak: read studio.gesture.active during the gesture and studio.dock.state after it. A test that a scrub did not move a panel is then two string reads, not a screenshot comparison.

open_questions.question: Is preference_client.rs operator-scoped or workspace-scoped? L1 and L2 of the persistence cascade require an operator-scoped, workspace-independent store. If it is workspace-scoped, either it needs an operator key namespace or the cascade needs a fourth store, before Studio ships.

Two left rails - the shell activity rail plus Studio's tool rail - consume 76px before any content. Acceptable, or should Studio's tools be injected as a section INTO the shell rail (one rail, mode-dependent contents)? Injecting is cleaner spatially but couples Studio to shell chrome and makes the tool rail disappear when the shell rail is used for navigation.

Does Studio ship a Generate panel at all? The Dreamweaver and Premiere captures carry an explicit excluded_ai policy; the Photoshop and Illustrator captures do not, and both ship generative surfaces. If yes, does it route to Handshake's own ModelRuntime rather than any vendor service?

Is the preset-library merge (12 vendor surfaces to 1 kind-filtered panel) acceptable, given it depends entirely on multi-instance support to avoid regressing simultaneous visibility? Rejecting it raises the panel count from 75 to about 84 and simplifies the panel widget considerably.

Should a document-type switch between Studio tabs animate the layout change or apply it instantly? Animation reads as intentional and reversible; instant reads as fast but is easy to mistake for a glitch. This is the one moment Studio's whole arrangement changes, so how it reads matters more than usual.

After Effects has no captured workspace file. The motion default layout is extrapolated from Premiere's dvaui evidence. Should an AE workspace capture be added to the greenroom before the motion layout is treated as settled?
Lightroom Classic likewise has no captured panel layout. The photo layout leans on develop parameters and Affinity's photo-side workspaces. Same question.

RESOLVED BY OUI-002. The fixed 2x2 is a recorded defect and replacing it with the egui_tiles tree is a microtask. Remaining sub-question: does the shell's non-Studio use of split_layout.rs migrate onto Studio's centre tree in the same work packet, or a follow-on? This proposal recommends a follow-on so the two migrations do not block each other, with split_layout.rs deleted when its last caller is gone.

Confirm the scrub modifier keys. Proposed: Shift = coarse x10, Alt = fine x0.1, Shift+Alt = x0.01. Alt is proposed for fine rather than Ctrl because Ctrl is a menu accelerator prefix and OUI-006 makes the menu load-bearing. Already listed in operator-ui-requirements.json open_for_operator_decision.

Wheel default over a dense panel. OUI-008 states the wheel over a field steps the value, but in a panel that is mostly fields this makes wheel-scrolling the panel nearly impossible. Proposed mitigation is a reserved 10px scroll lane plus wheel-over-label scrolling, keeping the operator's stated behaviour intact. The alternative is to invert the default (wheel scrolls, modifier+wheel steps). Which?

Is a 24px scrub row acceptable, or does the operator want the denser 20px vendor row with a smaller grab target? 24px costs about 20 percent of the visible parameter count per group; 20px risks missed grabs. This is the single biggest density lever in the proposal.

Does the operator want cross-document-type named presets (an arrangement that survives switching from raster to vector), or is per-type strictly correct? Per-type is proposed because it is what every vendor does, but the operator's tab-heavy workflow might argue otherwise.

Cap of 5 tabs for auto-resolved inspector siblings: is that the right number? Premiere ships a 13-tab group, so the platform tolerates depth, but 13 auto-generated tabs would be unreadable. The number is a judgement, not evidence.

risks.risk: The preset-library merge regresses simultaneous visibility. In Photoshop the operator can see swatches, gradients and patterns at once; under the merge he sees one at a time unless multi-instance works.
risks.mitigation: Multi-instance support (studio.panel.preset-library#2) is a HARD requirement of the merge, not an enhancement. If multi-instance slips, un-merge the panel before shipping. Also: the panel's kind selector should be a persistent row of icons, not a dropdown, so switching kinds costs one click.

risks.risk: The contextual inspector thrashes. Every selection change reshuffles the right column, the operator loses their place, and the AccessKit tree churns so GUI tests become flaky.
risks.mitigation: The three anti_thrash_rules (sticky active tab keyed by primitive, resolution on selection-change only, stable ranks 2..5). Plus a hard test: a GUI validation case that selects, deselects and reselects the same node and asserts the emitted AccessKit tree is byte-identical.

risks.risk: Two left rails plus a browse dock leave too little canvas on a laptop display. 44 + 32 + 260 = 336px of left chrome before the document.
risks.mitigation: The left dock starts COLLAPSED for raster, vector and photo - the three types where vendors themselves ship no left dock. Below a width threshold, auto-collapse the shell rail to icons and the Studio browse dock to its icon rail, and surface a 'focus mode' command that collapses every edge to rails in one action. See OQ-2.

risks.risk: Five separate egui_tiles trees drift out of sync during a cross-tree drag - a tile removed from the source and never inserted into the target, losing the panel.
risks.mitigation: PanelMoveRequest is applied as a single transaction against the StudioPanelRegistry FIRST (which owns the truth about where every panel is), and the trees are rebuilt from the registry, rather than mutating the two trees directly. The registry can then assert that every registered panel appears in exactly one tree, every frame in debug builds.

risks.risk: Panel author_ids leak into persisted layouts, then a panel is renamed or merged and every saved layout silently loses it.
risks.mitigation: author_ids are frozen on first ship and carry an alias table for merges (e.g. gradients -> preset-library?kind=gradient). Restore drops unknown ids with a log line rather than failing, exactly as layout_persistence.rs already handles a missing pane. Add the alias table to the same schema so it versions with the layout.

risks.risk: The 75-panel count is treated as a work estimate. It is a count of identities, not of implementation effort - effect-controls alone subsumes nine InDesign surfaces and the entire After Effects effect catalogue.
risks.mitigation: Any downstream work packet must size from the capability registry's 40798 capabilities mapped through these panels, not from the panel count. State this explicitly in the work packet that consumes this proposal.

risks.risk: module_switcher.rs's module_tab_list() rewrites the active pane's tab list on every module switch. If Studio documents are modelled as PaneTypes, switching to Studio and back could destroy the operator's open document set.
risks.mitigation: Model Studio documents as a single PaneType::StudioViewport with content_id carrying the document id, so module_tab_list sees one stable tab. Studio's own document tab strip manages the document set independently of the module machinery. Add a regression test that switches MAIN -> STUDIO -> MAIN with three Studio documents open and asserts all three survive.

risks.risk: Dreamweaver's priority semantics are INFERRED, not documented in the capture. If higher-wins is backwards, every binding priority in Studio is inverted.
risks.mitigation: The inference is supported by two independent internal patterns (div at 1 as catch-all versus div at 50 for six widgets; META at 5 versus four refined META variants at 6) and no counterexample was found in the 60 declarations. Nevertheless, the resolver should be written with the comparator as a single named function so an inversion is a one-line change, and a fixture test should encode the six div bindings and assert spry_accordion wins over spry_widget.

risks.risk: The right dock's three-group default is derived from Affinity's modal answer (6 of 9 workspaces). Premiere's own default (EDITING) uses one tall right pane. Studio may be imposing a page-design habit on video work.
risks.mitigation: Already handled: the video default layout uses TWO right groups, transcribed from Premiere's EDITING workspace, rather than three. The three-group default applies to the page-design types where its evidence comes from.

risks.risk: Auto-expand of the bottom dock on a job result steals focus and layout space mid-gesture - the exact class of interruption the shell's quiet-mode discipline exists to prevent.
risks.mitigation: Auto-expand is per-panel opt-in, never steals keyboard focus, never fires while a pointer drag is in progress, and is globally disableable. Route it through the existing quiet_mode module rather than reimplementing the policy.

risks.risk: The operator's requirement that panels move across all four sides is satisfiable, but a panel designed for a 300px-wide right dock renders badly in a 240px-tall bottom dock.
risks.mitigation: Every panel declares min_width, min_height and a preferred_orientation (vertical, horizontal, either). Photoshop's own workspace files carry preferred_unconstrained_size and preferred_constrained_size per placement - the vendor solved this by declaring sizes, and Studio should copy that field rather than invent one. A panel dropped into an orientation it declares as unsupported still docks, but renders a compact fallback layout.

risks.risk: A scrub drag that starts in a field but continues over a tab strip or a dock edge triggers a panel move, tab reorder or dock resize. The operator tries to nudge an X value and loses their panel arrangement.
risks.mitigation: pointer_gesture_arbitration rules 1, 2 and 4 together: claim at press with no threshold, panel and tab drags only from designated chrome, and total suppression of every other hover and drop target for the duration of a captured gesture. Test: a scripted press inside studio.field.transform.x followed by motion across studio.tabs.right.1 and studio.split.right.1 and release, asserting studio.dock.state is byte-identical before and after and studio.gesture.active read 'scrub' throughout.

risks.risk: Panel density and scrubbability are in direct conflict. Making every field grabbable costs vertical space, so a right dock shows meaningfully fewer parameters than the vendor product it replaces, and the operator experiences Studio as cramped.
risks.mitigation: Quantified rather than hand-waved: panel_density_model derives a 300px right dock from Illustrator's own measured 240px floor plus a 32px scrub allowance, and shows the resulting 9-row group height agrees with Illustrator's own declared 298px Transform panel height. The residual cost is real - roughly 20 percent fewer visible rows at 24px pitch than at the vendor's 20px - and is surfaced to the operator as OQ-13 rather than absorbed silently. Secondary mitigation: linked pairs (X/Y, W/H) share a row, recovering most of the loss on the geometry panels where it bites hardest.

risks.risk: The scrub cursor and the dock-splitter cursor look the same, so the operator cannot tell a value from a divider and drags the wrong one.
risks.mitigation: Distinct cursor assignment (splitters ResizeHorizontal/ResizeVertical, fields ResizeColumn), an 8px inset between a field's hit rect and any splitter hit strip, and a custom scrub cursor if the two still read alike in practice. This is a genuine consequence of OUI-008's requirement that the field advertise draggability with a resize cursor.

risks.risk: The wheel mitigation fails in practice: the 10px scroll lane is too narrow to hit reliably, and the operator finds dense panels unscrollable.
risks.mitigation: Wheel also scrolls over labels, group headers, separators and any blank area, so the lane is a guarantee rather than the only target. If it still fails, OQ-12's inversion is the fallback and is a one-line default change, not a redesign.

risks.risk: The centre editor tree being unbounded (OUI-002) makes the persisted layout unbounded too, and a session with many groups produces a large AccessKit tree that slows the out-of-process inspector.
risks.mitigation: accessibility/snapshot.rs already caps snapshots at MAX_SNAPSHOT_NODES; Studio must respect that cap and report truncation explicitly rather than silently. The editor tree persists as egui_tiles' own serde form, which is compact. No group cap is imposed, because OUI-002 forbids one.

risks.risk: Vendor evidence is treated as user evidence. What Adobe shipped as a default is not proof that the operator prefers it - it is proof of what the field converged on, which is a weaker claim.
risks.mitigation: Stated here explicitly. Every placement in this proposal is traceable to a counted vendor fact, and every such fact is one the operator can overrule in one drag, with L2 persistence making the overrule permanent. The defaults are a starting position, not an argument.
